title: UKPNP International Conference on Jammu Kashmir at House of Commons, London
excerpt: A landmark international conference by UKPNP at the House of Commons highlighting Kashmir as a human rights issue and calling for reunification and self-determination.
author: Special Correspondent

body.text: UKPNP International Conference on Jammu Kashmir in House of Commons UK

Press Release London UK July 8th, 2025. Special Correspondent The Mirror Jammu Kashmir London UK. UKPNP International Conference on Jammu Kashmir in House of Commons UK 8th July 2025. Houses of Parliament, London, under the theme: Kashmir Conflict: Peace, Security and Fundamental Rights in Jammu and Kashmir.

LONDON, July 8, 2025 The United Kashmir People’s National Party (UKPNP) held a landmark International Kashmir Conference in the Boothroyd Room of the Houses of Parliament, London, under the theme Kashmir Conflict: Peace, Security and Fundamental Rights in Jammu and Kashmir, where exiled Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri declared that Kashmir is not a territorial dispute between India and Pakistan but a matter of life, identity, and dignity for millions of Kashmiris, demanding the reunification of the forcibly divided state as a peaceful, autonomous buffer zone between three nuclear powers.
Kashmir is not a territorial or bilateral issue. It is an international issue. The future of Jammu and Kashmir must be determined by its people not by force or external diktats.

body.caption: Panel discussion at House of Commons

body.text: The conference, hosted by Labour MP for Leeds East and former Shadow Secretary of State for Justice Richard Burgon, saw extensive participation from Members of the British Parliament, international human rights activists, legal experts, academics, Kashmiri and oppressed nations leaders, media professionals, and diaspora representatives. The chief guest and keynote speaker was Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, Exiled Chairman of UKPNP and Administrative Director of CIRAC to the United Nations in Geneva and New York. The event was presided over by Sardar Tariq Khan, President of UKPNP United Kingdom, and moderated by Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan, Central Spokesperson of UKPNP and Main Representative to the UN in Geneva and New York.
UKPNP has consistently and categorically opposed all forms of violence, terrorism, religious extremism, and the dangerous weaponization of faith.
Distinguished MPs present included Fabian Hamilton MP, Imran Hussain MP, and Ian Byrne MP along with leading international speakers, legal experts, activists, and representatives.
Kashmir is one of the world’s longest unresolved conflicts, which must be resolved peacefully according to the will of the Kashmiri people.
Condemnation of Pahalgam Attack and Extrajudicial Killings

Statements from MPs emphasized peaceful resolution and human rights. Numerous resolutions were presented by Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri and unanimously adopted, including demands for investigation into the Pahalgam attack, an end to extrajudicial killings, release of political prisoners, reunification of Jammu and Kashmir, and international monitoring.
Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri strongly condemned the Pahalgam terror attack and the extrajudicial killings of Zarnosh Nasim and Jibran Nasim, demanding accountability and judicial inquiry.
UKPNP demands an immediate end to extrajudicial killings, torture, enforced disappearances, and arbitrary use of anti-terrorism laws.

The conference adopted a comprehensive 28 point resolution declaring the Kashmir conflict a human rights issue and calling for reunification as a buffer state between India, Pakistan, and China. It urged the United Nations and international community to take active steps.
There is no military solution to this conflict. Only justice, dialogue, and international law can ensure peace.
The conference reaffirmed commitment to democracy, human rights, freedom of expression, and peaceful resolution, calling for global cooperation and monitoring mechanisms.

The UKPNP reaffirmed its peaceful democratic struggle for reunification. The conference marked a major milestone in uniting global voices for justice, peace, and fundamental rights in Jammu and Kashmir.
